findings.description: `--tier` changed from `default="unverified"` to `default=None` while the documented API transport default remains `unverified`. Unless every API path below now normalizes `None` before use, invoking the probe with the default `--transport api` no longer supplies the intended tier and can either omit the request tier or fail validation downstream.
findings.failure_mode: A default API probe run behaves differently from the CLI contract: `--tier` is no longer `unverified` by default, so the transport may use an unintended account tier or reject the call, violating the documented flag behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep argparse default as `"unverified"` for API transport, or normalize `args.tier = "unverified"` before any API transport logic while still rejecting `--tier` for `claude-headless` if that is required.

findings.description: (Content is tools/ceiling-probe-live.py despite the diff header.) The throttle-wins precedence `_THROTTLE.search(full) and (is_context_limit_message(full) or is_token_limit_message(full))` is now evaluated over `full`, which concatenates the error `result`, the api_status tag and the ENTIRE stderr (up to 1 MB); previously only 300 chars were examined. Any `throttl`, `please wait`, `rate limit`, `tokens per min` or bare `429` anywhere in stderr (wrapper banner, CLI notice, an unrelated earlier log line) flips a genuine context-limit rejection into `transient token_limit`, costing up to 4 attempts / 140 s per step, and if it persists it is recorded as `failure_class: token_limit`, which forces outcome `partial` even though the real bracket was a context-limit rejection. Separately, the bare-429 alternative `(?<![\d,.])429(?![\d,.])` also rejects a sentence-final period, so `... returned status 429.` is not recognised as a throttle marker.
findings.failure_mode: A real size rejection is retried on the TPM schedule and then mis-bracketed; a clean probe degrades to `partial` for a reason unrelated to the model; a 429 that ends a sentence loses the throttle precedence and may be classified as a size rejection with no retry (the exact r251-1 regression the rule was added to prevent).
findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate the throttle precedence on the structured error only (`result` + api_status), or require the throttle marker within a short window (e.g. 200 chars) of the context/token marker rather than anywhere in 1 MB of stderr. Change the 429 lookahead to `(?!\d|[,.]\d)` so trailing punctuation is allowed while `429,000` / `429.5` are still excluded. Add tests: a context-limit `result` with stderr containing "please wait" must classify `size`; "status 429." must match the throttle marker.

findings.cross_file_justification: `_run_capped` (in the diff) replaced `subprocess.run(input=bytes, timeout=)` with `run_subprocess_pgkill(cmd, input=prompt, ..., max_bytes=_CAPTURE_CAP)` from loa_cheval.providers.base. The input is now a str, and the failure contract changed: the helper raises `SubprocessOutputCapExceeded` on the cap and whatever it raises on timeout, which may not be `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`. The step loop that must map these to an `other` sample is not in the diff.
findings.description: The docstring promises a timeout kills the process group and that output past the cap 'maps to `other`', but the mapping lives in the step loop outside the diff. The unit tests described in the report stub `_run_capped` with canned (rc, stdout, stderr), and the only live run (Task 1.5) predates this change, so the new `run_subprocess_pgkill` integration has never executed against a real CLI. Two things are unverified: (1) the helper accepts a str `input` (the old code passed bytes); (2) the step catches the helper's actual exception types rather than `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`.
findings.failure_mode: If the step still catches only `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, a CLI timeout propagates as an unexpected exception: the bisection ends with `stop: interrupted`, exit 1, and the attempt is charged as interrupted rather than recorded as a timeout `other` sample at the same size. If the helper expects bytes, every attempt fails before spawn and the probe never runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm `run_subprocess_pgkill`'s input type and the exact exceptions it raises on timeout and on the cap; make the step catch exactly those (and `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` for safety) and record `other` with `timeout: true` / `output_cap_exceeded: true` charged at the estimate. Add one test that patches `run_subprocess_pgkill` to raise each exception and asserts an `other` sample is recorded and the bisection continues/stops per spec, not an interrupted record.

findings.description: `--tier` default changed from `"unverified"` to `None` so the headless transport can detect an explicitly passed api-only flag. The api-transport write path in the same file (not in the diff) previously received the string and wrote/compared it. The help text promises "(default unverified)" but no `args.tier or "unverified"` substitution is visible in the diff.
findings.failure_mode: A default `--transport api --write-catalog` run writes `tier: None` into the catalog (or fails a `_TIERS` lookup/validation) at the write step, after the paid bisection has completed. The report's claim 'API path unchanged' does not cover a run with no `--tier` if the test passes `--tier` explicitly.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve `tier = args.tier if args.tier is not None else "unverified"` once at the top of the api branch (or set the default inside the api dispatcher) and add an api-path test that runs with no `--tier` and asserts the written tier is `unverified`.

findings.description: `probe_outcome` and `sample_size` are new REQUIRED keyword-only parameters with no defaults, and the function raises ValueError for anything but `clean`/`partial` or a non-int sample size. It is invoked at the very end of a paid run by `_main_cli` (not in the diff) and was also used ad hoc by the lead for the Task 1.5 write. Any caller still on the old signature raises TypeError at that point; a `partial` outcome without `force_partial` raises ValueError. The docstring says the catalog is never written on interrupt but says nothing about an exception raised by the catalog write itself after a completed bisection.
findings.failure_mode: A `--write-catalog` run completes the bisection (spend incurred), then crashes with TypeError/ValueError at the write. If the record is written only after the catalog write, the record is lost too and the spend has no artefact.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify `_main_cli` passes `probe_outcome=record["outcome"]`, `sample_size=len(accepted)+len(rejected)` and `force_partial=args.write_partial_as_operator_set`. Write the record BEFORE attempting the catalog write and wrap the write so a ValueError/TypeError is reported (exit 1) with the record intact. Add a `_main_cli` clean-path test that goes through `--write-catalog` end to end rather than calling `write_catalog_operator_set` directly.

findings.description: The new TPM rule says a token-budget 429 that persists 'once the window was waited out' is a size rejection (`failure_class: token_limit`), but the same spec caps total sleep per step at `_RETRY_WAIT_CAP_S = 180` and honours a `retry-after` hint only 'when longer' up to that cap. When the hint exceeds the remaining cap (org-level ITPM pressure regularly yields hints above 60 s), the window has NOT been waited out, yet the persisting 429 still becomes a size rejection that steers the bisection downward. Separately, a `token_limit` size rejection reflects the account's per-minute budget, not the model's context window. The record's `partial` outcome and the catalog's new `probe_outcome: partial` do not say which failure class bracketed the bound, so an operator using `--write-partial-as-operator-set` cannot see that the bound is TPM-shaped.
findings.failure_mode: A bound that is an artefact of the account's ITPM rather than the model's ceiling is written as `operator_set` and governs production routing; with a long retry-after the bisection moves below the true ceiling without ever having retried outside the window.
findings.suggested_fix: When the hint exceeds the remaining cap, classify the persisting 429 as `other` (transient exhausted), not `size`. Record the bracketing `failure_class` in the record and in `ceiling_calibration` (e.g. `bracket: context_limit | token_limit`), and refuse or loudly warn on `force_partial` when the bracket is `token_limit`.

findings.description: The diff header names `.claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_probe_cli_transport.py` (index 6e084077..8e034532) but every hunk is `tools/ceiling-probe-live.py`: the module docstring, `_run_capped`, `_classify`, `_classify_unguarded`, `write_catalog_operator_set` and `main`'s argparse. The test-file changes the report credits for r251-1 (TPM backoff schedule, throttle-vs-context precedence, interrupt record, pgkill, api-flag usage errors, required `probe_outcome`/`sample_size`) are therefore not in the review bundle, and the production tool is being reviewed under a test-file path.
findings.failure_mode: The r251-1 behaviours ship with unreviewed and possibly absent tests; review anchors resolve to the wrong file, so findings cannot be traced to the real location.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate the review diff from the commit for both paths (`git show 059e26be -- tools/ceiling-probe-live.py .claude/adapters/tests/test_ceiling_probe_cli_transport.py`) and rerun the review on the test file to confirm coverage of each r251-1 behaviour listed above.
